svg.aria-label: A user network on VLAN 42 added on zcore and advertised by the T1, a NETWORK42 portgroup on VLAN 42 in the zPod vCenter, a nested zbox deployed on it at 192.168.42.10, and the SSH path to it
svg.text: lab routers learn the T0 routes
VLANs 1–4094: VLAN 42 reaches zcore and every host
a VDS, uplinks vmnic0 · vmnic1 (recommended), or the existing vSwitch0
Every hop is routed: no NAT. With routing local instead of global, only the zPod reaches 192.168.42.0/24.
Add the network on zcore, then advertise it
zcli zpod network add demo --name net42
zcli zpod network routing demo net42 global
no overlap with the zPod or its endpoint pool
global: superadmin only; the flow checks
the whole fabric for overlaps first
Create the portgroup in the zPod vCenter
Build a VDS, uplinks vmnic0 · vmnic1 (recommended),
or use the existing vSwitch0 of every host;
then add NETWORK42, VLAN 42, on either one
it exists: zPodFactory never creates one
a standard one is on every host of Cluster
Add zbox nested, on that portgroup
zcli zpod component add demo -c zbox-13.7.1
VLAN 42 has a zPod network: net42
host id 2–254 on it (.1 is zcore)
--vlan-id is for trunks and ESXi images
no --vnics: one portgroup for every NIC
root or zadmin, with the zPod password
--vlan-id makes the guest tag its own frames. It needs
a trunk portgroup, and an image that reads {{zpod_vlan}},
like ESXi. zbox doesn’t: the API refuses it (422).
